question.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>Cr</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>7</mn></msub></math> paper acidified with dilute <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>SO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> turns green when exposed to

solution.text:
Carbon dioxide and sulphur trioxide cannot undergo oxidation. Potassium dichromate is reduced to chromic sulphate in the presence of sulphur dioxide. The orange solution of potassium dichromate becomes green colour chromic sulphate.

K2Cr2O7 + 3SO2 + H2SO4 → K2SO4 + Cr2(SO4)3 + H2O

Hence, the gas is sulphur dioxide.
